1099-1110, 17,151 km2; the infobox gives no area to compare. Edessa, Saruj, Samosata and the Euphrates towns are inside, Harran is outside (the Harran page has Baldwin besiege it in 1104 rather than hold it). Birecik is drawn from 1099 but the Baldwin II page dates its acquisition to 1117; at 250 km2 per cell this is probably the river edge, so the shape stands.

region.text: Edessa, with Turbessel and Ravendel (Baldwin II page)

ledger.note: 1098: Baldwin of Boulogne founds the County of Edessa, the first crusader state. March 1098: Thoros 'was removed from power' and Baldwin succeeded him; the Baldwin II page adds that he 'seized Ravendel, Turbessel, and Edessa' in early 1098. The page gives the cities, not a boundary.

1100: Baldwin of Boulogne leaves for Jerusalem and Baldwin of Bourcq becomes count. He 'granted him the County of Edessa' before leaving on 2 October 1100; the house of Boulogne gives way to Bourcq within the same state.

region.text: the Harran plains, raided and besieged by Baldwin in 1104

ledger.counterpart: Jikirmish of Mosul and Sokman of Mardin
ledger.note: 1104: Baldwin besieges Harran. The Harran page has Baldwin 'besieged Harran earlier in 1104'; the Baldwin II page has his troops raiding the Harran plains. No ground changed hands; the zone is the fought-over plain.

region.text: the plain where the crusaders were routed

ledger.counterpart: Jikirmish of Mosul and Sokman of Mardin
ledger.note: 7 May 1104: Baldwin and Joscelin are captured at Harran. 'Seljuk victory'; the page says the county 'never really recovered and survived until 1144 but only because of divisions among the Muslims' and does not say that any county land was lost.

region.text: the northern strip Cliopatria adds in 1111, without Raban and Kaisun (1116)

ledger.note: Page silent: Cliopatria's 1111 shape adds a strip north to 38.4 N (Kesoun, Raban, Behesni, Hisn Mansur). The Baldwin II page dates only Raban and Kaisun, to 1116, so this event is a bridge and the 1116 event replaces its Raban and Kesoun part.

region.text: Raban and Kaisun, which Baldwin 'forced his prisoner to renounce in 1116'

ledger.counterpart: Vasil Dgha (Armenian lord of Kesoun and Raban)
ledger.note: 1116: Baldwin takes Raban and Kaisun. He 'forced his prisoner to renounce Raban and Kaisun in 1116'; the coordinates are approximate.

region.text: Birejik, 'granted ... to Waleran of Le Puiset'

ledger.note: 1117: Birecik surrenders after a siege of about a year. 'Ablgharib was forced into surrender in 1117' and Baldwin granted the fortress to Waleran of Le Puiset; Cliopatria draws the river edge from 1099.

1119: Joscelin of Courtenay becomes count. Baldwin became King of Jerusalem on 2 April 1118; after the Field of Blood (28 June 1119) and 'before leaving Antioch, he granted the County of Edessa to Joscelin of Courtenay'; the county page says 'Joscelin was given Edessa in 1119'. The house of Bourcq gives way to Courtenay within the same state.

region.text: the strip Cliopatria adds in 1126, bbox east to 39.8 E

ledger.note: Page silent: no page opened dates an acquisition near 1126; the county article gives none before 1144. The event bridges the Cliopatria shape and a gap-filler should open 'Joscelin I, Count of Edessa'.

region.text: Edessa and the lands east of the Euphrates, except Saruj (lost January 1145)

ledger.note: 24 December 1144: Zengi takes Edessa. 'part of the wall near the Gate of the Hours collapsed on 24 December'; 'The citadel was handed over on 26 December.' Joscelin II falls back to Turbessel and 'continued to rule his lands west of the Euphrates'; Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1146.
1144: the count's seat moves from Edessa to Turbessel (infobox: Turbessel 1144-1146 and 1146-1150).
January 1145: Zengi takes Saruj. 'In January 1145, Zengi captured Saruj and besieged Birejik', but the army of Jerusalem arrived and joined Joscelin; Birecik held.

27 October 1146: Joscelin II breaks into Edessa. 'Joscelin broke into the city on 27 October, taking advantage of the cooperation of the Edessene citizens'; the citadel stayed with Zengi's garrison. The county page says September 1146, the siege page October.

region.text: Edessa, lost again to Nur ad-Din

ledger.note: November 1146: Nur ad-Din drives Joscelin out of Edessa after the battle of 3 November (Joscelin II page). Edessa was never recovered.

region.text: Turbessel and the rest of the county

ledger.note: 1150: Joscelin II's wife sells Turbessel and the rest of the county to Manuel I. 'Joscelin's wife sold Turbessel and the rest of the county to Manuel I Comnenus' after Nur ad-Din captured Joscelin; the same page says the lands were conquered by Nur ad-Din and the Sultan of Rum within a year, so this is a paper transfer. Reviewer me-09-b: neither the County page ('His wife sold Turbessel and what was left of the county to the Byzantine Emperor Manuel I Comnenus', no year) nor the Joscelin II page (no year for the sale) dates it; 1150 is inferred from Joscelin's capture in spring 1150, and the Joscelin II page has Turbessel holding out under Joscelin III until it 'fell to Nur ad-Din's captain Hassan in 1151'. Confidence lowered to 1.

1151: the last of the county falls. Turbessel 'fell to Nur ad-Din's captain Hassan in 1151' and the county 'was invaded on all sides and mostly absorbed by Mesud, Timurtash of Mardin, and Nur ad-Din'. The page does not say which places went to whom.

wars.name: Battle of Harran

zones.text: the plain opposite Raqqa where the battle was fought

wars.outcome: Seljuk victory on 7 May 1104: Baldwin II and Joscelin were captured; Tancred became regent of Antioch and of Edessa. The page reports no loss of county land.
wars.note: The body puts the battle on the plain opposite Raqqa about two days from Harran; the infobox says Sanliurfa.

wars.name: Mosul and Artuqid attacks on Edessa
wars.outcome: Sokman attacked Saruj in early 1101; Mawdud besieged Edessa in April 1110 and April-June 1112 and Turbessel in July 1111; Aqsunqur invaded in May 1114. Edessa was never taken and no land changed hands.

wars.name: Siege of Edessa (1144)

zones.text: Edessa and the lands east of the Euphrates, including Saruj

wars.outcome: Zengi besieged Edessa from 28 November 1144, entered on 24 December and took the citadel on 26 December; he took Saruj in January 1145. Joscelin II kept the lands west of the Euphrates.

wars.name: Siege of Edessa (1146)
wars.outcome: Joscelin II retook the city but not the citadel on 27 October; Nur ad-Din drove him out in November. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Conquest of the county by Nur ad-Din and Mas'ud

zones.text: the remnants west of the Euphrates

wars.outcome: Nur ad-Din captured Joscelin II in 1150; Turbessel and the rest were sold to Manuel I, then fell in 1151 to Nur ad-Din's captain Hassan, Mesud and Timurtash of Mardin.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by any page; the county was a chain of towns and fortresses (Edessa, Saruj, Samosata, Turbessel, Birecik) whose outline is approximate throughout.

notes: Page budget: 5 pages for 5 shapes; six were opened because the first Siege of Edessa link was a disambiguation page. Unsettled: (1) no page opened dates the 1111 strip (Behesni, Hisn Mansur) or the 1126 growth; both are confidence-1 bridges, a gap-filler should open 'Joscelin I, Count of Edessa' and 'Baldwin I of Jerusalem'. (2) Samosata, Saruj and Aintab are inside Cliopatria's 1099 shape but no page opened dates their acquisition. (3) Disagreement on the 1146 recapture: county page 'Sept. 1146', siege page 'October 1146', Joscelin II page '27 October'; the last is used. (4) Infobox: 'Conquered by Nur ad-Din Zengi, remainder sold to Manuel I Komnenos: 1144'; the dossier ends in 1151 as Cliopatria does and as the Joscelin II page has Turbessel fall. (5) The sale of 1150 is recorded as a loss to the Byzantine empire at confidence 2 although the same pages say the lands fell within a year; the Byzantine dossier (eu-05) and the Zengid dossier should record the 1151 passage of Turbessel. (6) Coordinates for Turbessel, Raban and Kesoun are approximate and the gazetteer lacks the names (Turbessel/Tell Bashir, Samosata/Samsat, Saruj/Suruc, Birecik, Raban/Araban, Kesoun/Keysun, Ravendan). (7) 'Edessa under Thoros' and the Artuqids (Sokman of Mardin, Timurtash) need dossiers.
